newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK sees China's military might at air show.
newsitem.headline: HK sees China's military might at air show.

text.p: Beijing put its fighter jets and helicopters on show on Thursday, allowing Hong Kong people a glimpse of the military hardware that will be used to defend the territory after it reverts to China in July.
Thousands of people flocked to the China Aviation Industry Show at the Hong Kong Convention Centre. The display, featuring military aircraft, is the biggest China has ever staged outside its borders.

"We have equipped the People's Liberation Army (PLA) with a large amount of aviation equipment," Zhu Yuli, president of Aviation Industries of China (AVIC), overseeing aviation- related industries, said as he opened the week-long show.

The show displayed helicopters, guided missiles and jets, including two recent models of the F7 and F8 fighters that will accompany the PLA garrison in Hong Kong after Britain returns it to China on July 1, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
Chinese military technology chief Wang Tongye told reporters the Chinese garrison to be stationed in Hong Kong would be armed with China's most advanced equipment.
"That represents the (military technology) level of our country," said Wang, the deputy director of the Commission of Science, Technology and Industry for National Defence.
The garrison to be stationed in the territory would have advanced helicopters in addition to warships, speedboats and light armour, but no tanks, he said.
Hong Kong people still shudder at the memory of PLA tanks thundering into Beijing's Tiananmen Square to crush student-led pro-democracy protests in 1989.

The Chinese also put on display a wide variety of products made by the aviation industry. Military units have turned their hand to civilian business in the swords-to-ploughshares trend of recent years -- including watches, motorcycles and photocopiers.
Hundreds of aircraft enthusiasts queued to enter the exhibition hall and to buy aircraft models and souvenirs.
"This show is not only the biggest exhibition that we ever held abroad since the founding of China's aviation industry 46 years ago, but an overview of the industry," Zhu said.

"China's aviation industry has developed into a high-tech industrial system with comprehensive disciplines and overall capabilities in military and civil production, scientific research, education and management," he said.

More than 14,000 military and commerical aircraft, about 15,000 tactical missiles, and more than 50,000 aero engines and their supporting airborne equipment had been made and delivered since the industry was founded in 1951, he said.
"We have already established economic and trade ties with over 70 countries and regions around the world.

"In addition to the joint development and production of commercial aircraft and helicopters together with foreign companies, the aviation industry also sees rapid growth on the subcontract of parts and components of aero products," Zhu said.
AVIC aimed for a 20 percent annual average growth rate in turnover, sales and revenue by the year 2000, he said.
The industry includes 110 industrial enterprises, 34 research institutes and seven universities and colleges.
